A_runtime.reason: This peer performed source review only. No browser, build, test, or service-error run was launched. Existing warm and reload observations do not establish the service-error dimension.

B_source.finding: The runner proves a real /health failure only during the Bridges probe. exerciseServiceError restores the owned side-panel target to online, re-enables cache, disables Network observation, and returns to Log before the natural public-page event generation and every Search, Pause/Resume, Clear, and detail control action. serviceErrorProved remains true, so scenarioEvidence can label those later healthy-network actions as serviceError pass despite no failure condition persisting through them.
B_source.positive_controls: The source checks a same-URL real panel GET with HTTP 200 and visible OK, then an actual Network.loadingFailed and visible FAIL under target-scoped offline conditions. It does not mock responses, inject events, write database data, use Chat/Pilot, or send Source Save input. The native harness owns the disposable browser profile.
B_source.restoration: The offline toggle is target-scoped and its restoration is in finally before ordinary controls. This bounds the outage safely but is also why those controls are not service-error evidence.
B_source.additional_limit: The health helper's failure is silent in the Debug event log. The failed ping does not establish a natural error row or positive error badge; T17 badge clearing still requires its separate pre-Clear positive control.
B_source.required_correction: Keep the actual service-error condition present and independently observable while each relevant Debug control runs, then restore the owned target's network in an outer finally. Alternatively, keep all four service-error dimension results unverified and use the current probe only as a precondition check. Do not promote an earlier FAIL label after restoration into during-error evidence.
